# Adjust Video Brightness & Color

- Route: `/tools/adjust-video-color`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `video`
- Slug: `adjust-video-color`

## Summary

Brighten a dark clip, add contrast and saturation, shift the hue, or apply a blur or artistic look, with sliders and a live preview. (Video tools)

## Details

A clip shot indoors comes out dark and orange; a flat phone video wants more contrast and colour; a clip for a thumbnail needs a stylised look. Media Manipulator applies brightness, contrast, saturation, hue, gamma and exposure corrections on our servers with FFmpeg, alongside blur, sharpening, grain and a set of artistic filters, and exports MP4. It is a colour correction pass without opening an editor.
### What it does
- Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue sliders from -100 to +100.
- Gamma, exposure, shadows and highlights for finer tonal control.
- Gaussian and motion blur, unsharp-mask sharpening, film grain and noise.
- Artistic looks such as oil painting, sketch and vintage.
- Combine with trim, resize, speed or flip in the same pass.
### How to use it
1. Upload a clip: Any common format.
2. Move the sliders: Brightness, contrast, saturation, hue and more.
3. Convert: FFmpeg applies the eq and effect filters.
4. Download: Save the graded MP4.
### Supported formats
- Input: mp4, mov, mkv, webm, avi, m4v, flv, wmv
- Output: mp4, webm, mov, mkv, gif
### Technical details
- Brightness, contrast, saturation and gamma map to FFmpeg's eq filter; hue uses the hue filter in degrees.
- Sharpening is unsharp with radius, amount and threshold; blur is gblur or a directional motion blur.
- For a 3D LUT, chroma key or per-clip grading on a timeline, use Darkroom.
### Use cases
- Brighten a dark clip: Lift exposure and shadows on indoor footage.
- Punch up a flat clip: Add contrast and saturation to a log-looking phone video.
- Fix a colour cast: Shift hue to take out an orange or green tint.
- Stylise for social: Apply vintage, sketch or oil-painting looks.
### FAQ
Q: Can I preview the result?
A: The sliders show their values; the full grade is applied on conversion. Trim to a few seconds to test quickly, then run the whole clip.
Q: Can I apply a LUT?
A: Not here. Darkroom, our multi-track editor, supports 3D LUTs and per-clip grading.
Q: Will this fix overexposed footage?
A: It can bring highlights down, but detail that was clipped to white cannot be recovered.
Q: Can I sharpen a soft clip?
A: Yes. Use the unsharp mask controls; for real detail recovery try AI video restoration.
